viewpoints.claim: Interaction transitions run 200ms or less with an ease-out curve so the interface feels immediate.

source.author: Rauno Freiberg
source.quote: Animation duration should not be more than 200ms for interactions to feel immediate

prefers: Keep interaction transitions at 200ms or less, never above 300ms
Use ease-out for entering elements
Use a custom cubic-bezier instead of the built-in curves
forbids: Slow transitions on hover, focus, open and close
Bounce or elastic easing on everyday controls

measure.what: Computed transition-duration and animation-duration on elements that change on :hover, :focus, [aria-expanded] or [data-state]; flag any over 300ms, warn over 200ms; ease-in on an entering element fails.
measure.mustFail: A button with transition: background 600ms ease-in-out.
measure.mustPass: The same button with transition: background 150ms ease-out.

exceptions: Toasts may run slower with a plain ease on purpose for tone
Large page or scene transitions and decorative loops sit outside the interaction budget
Exit animations can be a bit more relaxed

viewpoints.claim: Actions used many times a day, and anything keyboard-triggered, appear instantly without an enter animation.

source.author: Rauno Freiberg
source.quote: Actions that are frequent and low in novelty should avoid extraneous animations: opening a right click menu, deleting or adding items from a list, hovering trivial buttons

prefers: Show context menus, command palettes and list changes instantly
Leave keyboard-driven navigation unanimated
forbids: Opacity and scale fades on controls used hundreds of times a day

measure.what: Enter animations on [role=menu], [cmdk-root] and newly inserted list items (animation-name not none), and animation state diffed within 16ms of a dispatched key; which actions count as frequent comes from the journey.
measure.mustFail: A context menu opening with animation: fadeIn 200ms.
measure.mustPass: The same menu with animation: none on open and a fade only on close.

exceptions: macOS context menus fade out and blink the chosen item
Rare features may be theatrical (delight-impact curve)
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A landing page, a docs article and a one-time checkout have little that counts as a frequent action; only shortcut-like or keyboard-triggered navigation on them applies.

viewpoints.claim: Scale and fade motion starts near its resting size, in proportion to the trigger, never from zero or a heavy squash.

source.author: Rauno Freiberg
source.quote: Don't animate dialog scale in from 0 → 1, fade opacity and scale from ~0.8. Don't scale buttons on press from 1 → 0.8, but ~0.96, ~0.9, or so.

prefers: Enter dialogs and popovers from scale 0.8–0.97 with opacity
Press buttons to about scale 0.96–0.97
forbids: Press states that squash a button to 0.8 or below

measure.what: Parse @keyframes and WAAPI keyframes on dialogs, popovers and buttons and read the starting scale(); :active transforms below about 0.9 fail.
measure.mustFail: @keyframes pop { from { transform: scale(0) } } on a dialog, or :active { transform: scale(0.8) }.
measure.mustPass: from { transform: scale(0.95); opacity: 0 } and :active { transform: scale(0.97) }.

exceptions: Elements that genuinely originate from a point, such as a FAB expanding into a sheet, can grow from small

viewpoints.claim: Animate only transform and opacity, listing properties explicitly; never transition all or animate layout properties.

source.author: Emil Kowalski
source.quote: you should try to animate with `transform` and `opacity` as they only trigger the third rendering step (composite)

prefers: Prefer CSS, then WAAPI, then JS for motion
Use clip-path for reveals
List transitioned properties explicitly
forbids: Animating width, height, top, left, margin or padding
Large blur() values on filter or backdrop-filter in motion

measure.what: Scan stylesheets and computed transition-property for all and for layout properties; scan @keyframes for width, height, top and left.
measure.mustFail: .card { transition: all 200ms } or @keyframes grow { to { height: 300px } }.
measure.mustPass: transition: transform 200ms, opacity 200ms, or to { transform: scaleY(1) }.

exceptions: Accordion height animation via grid-template-rows or interpolate-size is layout by nature and accepted when it is the only honest way

viewpoints.claim: A popover or menu animates from the side facing its trigger; set transform-origin where the motion physically starts.

source.author: Emil Kowalski
source.quote: When we click on a button that opens a dropdown, we expect the dropdown to animate from where the button is

prefers: Set transform-origin toward the trigger
Use the anchoring library's origin variable when one exists
forbids: Popovers scaling from their own centre when anchored to a button

measure.what: For each open popover or menu with a known trigger (aria-controls or aria-haspopup), compare the computed transform-origin with the side facing the trigger.
measure.mustFail: A menu below a button with transform-origin: 50% 50%.
measure.mustPass: The same menu with transform-origin: top center or the Radix origin variable.

exceptions: Centred modals have no anchor; a centred origin is right there
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Docs pages rarely anchor custom popovers to a trigger beyond an occasional footnote or share menu, and a checkout or sign-up mostly uses native selects rather than anchored popovers.

viewpoints.claim: Every large motion has a reduced variant under prefers-reduced-motion; fade instead of slide rather than ignoring the setting.

source.author: Emil Kowalski
source.quote: our animations need to account for people who don't want animations

prefers: Provide a reduced variant such as a fade instead of a slide
Give autoplaying motion over five seconds pause, stop or hide controls
forbids: Large translate or scale motion that ignores the media query

measure.what: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and list elements whose computed animation-name or transition-property still includes translations over about 20px or durations above zero.
measure.mustFail: A hero that keeps a translateY(40px) fly-in under the emulated query.
measure.mustPass: The same page with a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block reducing it to opacity.

exceptions: Motion that is the content, such as a video or a chart drawing, is out of scope
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A docs page and a single-pass checkout rarely carry large decorative motion; only their smaller transitions are in scope.

viewpoints.claim: An open or close animation can be reversed mid-flight by the next input; nothing waits for a transition to finish.

source.author: Emil Kowalski
source.quote: Great animations are interruptible

prefers: Use CSS transitions that reverse mid-flight, or spring libraries
forbids: pointer-events: none locks while an animation plays
Keyframe-driven open and close that must finish before the next input

measure.what: Open a panel, immediately send the close input, sample the element's bounding box about 50ms later; if it is still growing the animation was not interruptible. Depends on timing tolerance.
measure.mustFail: A drawer using animation: slideIn 400ms with fill-mode forwards and a JS isAnimating guard.
measure.mustPass: The same drawer with transition: transform 250ms toggled by class.

exceptions: Destructive commits that fire only on gesture end are about triggering, not interruptibility
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Landing pages, docs pages and checkout flows rarely use slide-out panels or drawers; the check mostly applies to their occasional modal.

viewpoints.claim: Every interactive element has a hit box of at least 44px on touch and 24px on desktop, with 8px between neighbours.

source.author: Apple
source.quote: a button needs a hit region of at least 44x44 pt

prefers: Expand the hit area with padding while the icon stays 24px
Keep at least 8px between adjacent targets
forbids: Clickable boxes under 24x24 CSS px on desktop

measure.what: For every focusable or role=button|link|checkbox element take getBoundingClientRect (plus pseudo-element extension) at the mobile viewport; fail under 44 there and under 24 on desktop; gap under 8px fails.
measure.mustFail: A 16x16 icon button with no padding, or two 44px buttons 4px apart.
measure.mustPass: The same icon with padding: 14px, and buttons 8px apart.

exceptions: Inline text links inside paragraphs
Dense data grids where the row is the target

viewpoints.claim: Lists of interactive items have no dead gaps, labels share the control's hit target, and anything that looks clickable is clickable.

source.author: Rauno Freiberg
source.quote: Interactive elements in a vertical or horizontal list should have no dead areas between each element, instead, increase their `padding`

prefers: Fill list rows with padding rather than margin
Wrap inputs with label for
Give buttons a discernible background shape and fill
Disable pointer-events on decorative glows and gradients
forbids: Decorative layers that intercept pointer events over controls

measure.what: Adjacent role=menuitem or li>a rects with vertical gaps over 0; inputs with no associated label; absolutely positioned decorative layers with pointer-events auto over controls; div or span click handlers with no role.
measure.mustFail: A nav list with margin-bottom: 6px between anchors.
measure.mustPass: The same list with margin: 0; padding: 8px 12px.

exceptions: Intentional separators between groups
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A single-column checkout or sign-up form has few list-like interactive groups beyond an occasional radio or checkbox set.

viewpoints.claim: Body text sits at the platform default size, weights stay 400 or heavier, and weight never changes on hover.

source.author: Rauno Freiberg
source.quote: Font weights below 400 should not be used

prefers: 17px body on touch, 13px minimum on desktop UI
Weights between 400 and 700
Headings at weight 500–600
Minimise the number of typefaces
forbids: Weight swaps on hover or selected state

measure.what: Computed font-size and font-weight of every text node at a phone viewport; count distinct font-family stacks and warn above 2.
measure.mustFail: p { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 300 } at a phone viewport, or a:hover { font-weight: 600 }.
measure.mustPass: 16px at weight 400, with hover changing colour only.

exceptions: Captions and legal text may sit at the platform minimum
Display headings may use light weights at large sizes

viewpoints.claim: Inputs are at least 16px on phones, never autofocus on touch, and the page never disables zoom or blocks paste.

source.author: Rauno Freiberg
source.quote: Font size for inputs should not be smaller than 16px to prevent iOS zooming on focus

prefers: Set type, inputmode and autocomplete on every input
Use touch-action: manipulation on controls

measure.what: Computed font-size of input, select and textarea at a 390px viewport under 16px; viewport meta containing user-scalable=no; paste handlers that preventDefault; [autofocus] present at phone width.
measure.mustFail: An input at 14px on a 390px viewport.
measure.mustPass: The same input at 16px.

exceptions: Desktop-only admin tools
Autofocus on desktop with a single primary input
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A docs site's only input is its search box; dashboards are sometimes checked on a phone, but back-office admin tools are commonly desktop-only, per the viewpoint's own exception, so the phone-width checks do not apply there.

viewpoints.claim: Text meets 4.5:1 (3:1 when large or bold), status is never colour alone, and hover raises contrast rather than lowering it.

source.author: Apple
source.quote: Convey information with more than color alone

prefers: Pair status colour with text or an icon
Use semantic colour consistently
Provide light and dark variants for every custom colour

measure.what: Sample foreground and background of each text node (compositing translucent layers) and compute the WCAG ratio; fail under 4.5:1 (3:1 for 18pt or bold); warn on red/green/amber elements with no text or icon sibling; fail when :hover contrast drops.
measure.mustFail: #999 body text on #fff (2.8:1).
measure.mustPass: #595959 body text on #fff (7:1).

exceptions: Disabled controls
Decorative text
Logos

viewpoints.claim: Every focusable element shows a visible focus ring on :focus-visible, and no sticky or fixed element ever covers it.

source.author: Vercel Labs
source.quote: NEVER: `outline: none` without visible focus replacement

prefers: Style :focus-visible with box-shadow or outline plus outline-offset
forbids: outline: none or 0 with no replacement
Focus rings hidden under sticky headers

measure.what: Tab through every focusable element; diff the focused and unfocused rect or read computed outline and box-shadow under :focus-visible; check the focused rect is not intersected by position fixed or sticky elements above it.
measure.mustFail: button:focus { outline: none }.
measure.mustPass: button:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--ring) }.

viewpoints.claim: Feedback appears next to its trigger, forms mark the failing field and focus it, and submit buttons keep their label while busy.

source.author: Rauno Freiberg
source.quote: Display feedback relative to its trigger: Show a temporary inline checkmark on a successful copy, not a notification; Highlight the relevant input(s) on form error(s)

prefers: Inline checkmark on copy, aria-invalid on the failing field
aria-live polite for async results
Undo window over a confirm dialog
Spinner that keeps the button label
forbids: Something went wrong with no cause
Save next to Discard at equal weight
Button labels that vanish into a spinner

measure.what: After an invalid submit, [aria-invalid=true] exists and activeElement is the first invalid field; after submit the button is disabled or aria-busy within a frame with textContent unchanged; copy feedback inside the trigger's subtree; adjacent same-size destructive and primary buttons warn.
measure.mustFail: An invalid form submit that only raises a toast, or a submit button whose label is replaced by a spinner.
measure.mustPass: The same form marking the field aria-invalid and focusing it, with the button disabled and its label kept.

exceptions: Actions whose success is not likely, such as payments, should wait for the server
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A landing page usually has one action and little to submit, and a docs page's local feedback is mostly its code-copy button.

viewpoints.claim: Empty, sparse, dense, error and loading states are designed; skeletons match final layout and long content never overflows.

source.author: Vercel Labs
source.quote: MUST: Design empty/sparse/dense/error states

prefers: An empty state with a primary create action
Skeletons sized like real rows
min-w-0 and truncation on flex children

measure.what: Render with [], with 1 item, with 500 items and with a 300-character title; assert no horizontal overflow, no overlap, an actionable control in the empty state, and skeleton-to-loaded CLS under a threshold.
measure.mustFail: A list component that renders nothing for [].
measure.mustPass: The same component rendering a heading and a Create button for [].

viewpoints.kindsWhy: A landing page has no data-driven empty state, and a docs page mostly only needs the long-content and loading checks.

viewpoints.claim: Numbers in columns and timers use tabular figures, images carry dimensions, and nothing changes weight on hover.

source.author: Rauno Freiberg
source.quote: tabular figures should be applied with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, particularly in tables or when layout shifts are undesirable, like in timers

prefers: tabular-nums in tables, timers and prices
width and height on every img

measure.what: Numeric td cells whose computed font-variant-numeric lacks tabular-nums; img without width/height or aspect-ratio; sibling rect drift while a counter fixture runs.
measure.mustFail: 1,234.56 under default numerals.
measure.mustPass: The same cell with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

exceptions: Prose numbers

viewpoints.claim: All shadows on a page share one light direction and offset ratio, layered and tinted toward the background hue.

source.author: Josh W. Comeau
source.quote: every shadow on the page should share the same ratio

prefers: A tokenised elevation scale
Two to five layered shadows
Shadow colour matched to the background hue
forbids: Shadows with inconsistent x:y ratios across the page

measure.what: Collect every computed box-shadow; fail when offset signs mix across the page or distinct shadow strings exceed about 6; warn when shadow hue is far from the background hue with alpha above 0.5.
measure.mustFail: Cards with 0 -4px 8px and 4px 4px 8px on the same page.
measure.mustPass: All shadows with an x:y offset ratio of 1:2.

exceptions: Inset shadows for sunken fields
Glows meant as glows
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Docs pages are often flat with few or no shadows, and single-column checkout and sign-up forms rarely carry elevation.

viewpoints.claim: Separate groups with whitespace, a background shade or one shadow before reaching for borders; never nest outlined boxes.

source.author: Adam Wathan & Steve Schoger
source.quote: Use fewer borders

prefers: Whitespace or background-shade contrast between groups
A single shadow instead of an outline
forbids: Borders on every side of every row

measure.what: Nesting depth of elements with a visible border or box-shadow outline that contain further bordered elements; depth 3 or more warns; bordered siblings also separated by gap 16px or more are redundant.
measure.mustFail: section > .card > .card > .card all with 1px solid borders.
measure.mustPass: An outer section border only, with inner groups separated by 24px gap.

exceptions: Data tables
Form field outlines, which are signifiers

viewpoints.claim: Margins, padding and gaps come from a documented 4 or 8px scale; no ad-hoc values and no edges that almost align.

source.author: Stan Kirilov
source.quote: Pick your numbers, document them, and don't deviate. Inconsistent spacing is the fastest way to make a polished product feel amateur.

prefers: A 4/8-based scale expressed as tokens
Deliberate alignment to a grid, baseline or edge

measure.what: Collect computed margin, padding and gap; fail when the off-4px share exceeds 10% or distinct values exceed 12; warn when sibling left edges sit within 1–3px of each other but not equal.
measure.mustFail: Paddings of 13, 17 and 22px.
measure.mustPass: Paddings of 12, 16 and 24px.

exceptions: Optical alignment of ±1px when perception beats geometry, so ±1 warns rather than fails

viewpoints.claim: Use a short radius scale, and keep nested corners concentric: the child's radius is the parent's minus the padding.

source.author: Vercel Labs
source.quote: SHOULD: Nested radii: child ≤ parent; concentric

prefers: Inner radius equal to outer radius minus padding
A radius scale of two to four values
forbids: Child radius larger than the parent's
One radius applied to pills, cards, modals and avatars alike

measure.what: Count distinct computed border-radius values and warn above 6; for nested rounded boxes compare the child radius with parent radius minus parent padding and fail when the child is larger.
measure.mustFail: .card { border-radius: 8px; padding: 4px } .card img { border-radius: 16px }.
measure.mustPass: The same card with the img radius at 4px.

exceptions: Fully round elements (9999px, avatars) are exempt from the concentric arithmetic

viewpoints.claim: Density is value delivered per unit of time and space; respond within 100ms, show an indicator past a second, and never mistake whitespace for quality.

source.author: Matthew Ström-Awn
source.quote: UI density is the value a user gets from the interface divided by the time and space the interface occupies.

prefers: Gestalt grouping over more separators
Fast loads over more pixels
Indeterminate indicator from 1s, determinate progress from 10s
forbids: Feedback delayed past 100ms with nothing shown

measure.what: Time from click to first visible change: over 100ms with no feedback fails, over 1s with no indicator fails, over 10s with only a spinner warns; the spatial value numerator cannot be computed.
measure.mustFail: A 3s fetch with no indicator.
measure.mustPass: An aria-busy skeleton shown at 150ms.

exceptions: The audience sets the ceiling: a bond trader tolerates far more density than a second grader
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A landing page and a docs article are read rather than repeatedly used, and a checkout or sign-up is completed once, so the repeated-use density argument is weak there; only the response-timing checks apply.

viewpoints.claim: Flat styling keeps its signifiers: buttons have a fill or border, links are underlined or distinctly coloured, inputs show a boundary.

source.author: Kate Moran (NN/G)
source.work: Flat UI Elements Attract Less Attention and Cause Uncertainty
source.quote: participants spent 22% more time… looking at the pages with weak signifiers

prefers: Buttons with a discernible fill or border
Links underlined or in a distinct colour
Inputs with a visible boundary
forbids: Long shadows and other purely aesthetic depth

measure.what: For each button or role=button: background differs from parent, or border width above 0, or text colour is the accent, else fail; an in-text link with no text-decoration and colour close to the surrounding text fails.
measure.mustFail: <button style="background:none;border:0;color:inherit">Save</button>.
measure.mustPass: The same button with a fill.

exceptions: Toolbar icon buttons with tooltips and hover fills
Navigation bars recognised by position

viewpoints.claim: Cards are for browsing; use lists for searching and tables for comparing, and keep each card readable with one primary action.

source.author: Stan Kirilov
source.quote: Cards for browsing. Lists for searching. Tables for comparing.

prefers: Lists for ranked or homogeneous data, tables for comparison
Consistent card heights
The title as the link, with a pseudo-element extending the hit area
forbids: Card grids for search results and settings
More than 3 clickable elements per card

measure.what: Detect card grids (3+ siblings with equal border, shadow and radius); fail on text under 14px, over 3 interactive descendants per card, row heights differing over 20%, or an anchor wrapping more than heading plus paragraph.
measure.mustFail: Six identical 280px cards with 12px body text and a wrapping anchor.
measure.mustPass: The same data as a table, or a card with 14px text and a title link.

exceptions: Masonry where variable height is the design choice
Media browsing such as Netflix or Pinterest
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A multi-step checkout or sign-up rarely lays out a card grid; the rule applies only when options are chosen from cards, such as a plan or payment method.

viewpoints.claim: Icons carry labels, menus are named for what they hold, and no primary feature hides under More or an ellipsis.

source.author: Jakob Nielsen (NN/G)
source.quote: most icons, unless they have a text label next to them, will be difficult or impossible for users to understand

prefers: Labelled icons
Menus named for their contents
Inline help before tooltips
forbids: More, ellipsis or Tools catch-alls holding primary features

measure.what: Icon-only buttons with no text and no aria-label fail; menus triggered by More, …, Tools or Options holding over 5 items or a primary-action label warn; disabled buttons with title or aria-describedby fail.
measure.mustFail: <button><svg/></button>.
measure.mustPass: <button aria-label="Delete"><svg/></button>, better with visible text.

exceptions: Universally recognised icons in tight toolbars, though even the hamburger is weaker than designers think
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A simple checkout or sign-up form has few icon-only controls or catch-all menus to begin with.

viewpoints.claim: Translucency is for chrome over busy backgrounds with heavy blur and a contrast fallback, never for body content or decoration.

source.author: Megan Brown (NN/G)
source.quote: glassmorphism is best when utilized sparingly to create an illusion of depth

prefers: Glass on toolbars and menus only
Heavy blur over intricate backgrounds
A solid fallback under increased contrast
forbids: Text whose contrast depends on what scrolls beneath it
Glass with a neon glow as decoration

measure.what: For each element with backdrop-filter, sample contained-text contrast against the composited background at three scroll positions; any under 4.5:1 fails; blur under 12px over an image warns; body text over 2 lines inside glass warns.
measure.mustFail: .card { backdrop-filter: blur(4px); background: rgba(255,255,255,.2) } over a photo hero.
measure.mustPass: blur(24px) with rgba(255,255,255,.75) on a toolbar, or a solid fallback under prefers-contrast: more.

exceptions: OS-level materials that honour the user's Reduce Transparency setting
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Docs pages, product pages and single-purpose checkout or sign-up forms rarely use decorative glass chrome beyond an occasional sticky header or overlay.

viewpoints.claim: Opt-ins start unchecked, accept and decline are symmetric, cancelling is as easy as subscribing, and urgency is real.

source.author: Harry Brignull
source.quote: The user is presented with a default option that has already been selected for them, in order to influence their decision-making

prefers: Opt-in unchecked by default
Symmetric accept and decline buttons
Cancel as easy as subscribe
Countdowns that are real

measure.what: Checked checkboxes whose label matches a marketing or upsell lexicon fail; a decline button under 3:1 contrast or under 60% the accept's size warns; a countdown that restarts on reload fails; confirmshaming copy is lexical and only warns.
measure.mustFail: <input type=checkbox checked> Send me offers.
measure.mustPass: The same checkbox unchecked.

exceptions: Defaults that serve the user; who benefits is for the journey's actor to decide
viewpoints.kindsWhy: Dashboards and back-office admin tools rarely sell or upsell, a docs or blog page has at most a newsletter opt-in, and browsing or comparing on a catalogue page has fewer of these patterns than the cart and checkout step itself.

viewpoints.claim: Meeting the spec is the baseline, not the finish; ask whether it feels right, reduce scope to raise quality, use plain words.

source.author: Karri Saarinen
source.quote: Even we, as designers, stopped asking; 'Does this feel right?'

prefers: Treat the spec as the baseline, not the finish line
Reduce scope to increase quality
Call projects projects; plain vocabulary
forbids: Shipping to spec and calling it done
A/B tests standing in for judgement

measure.what: A person asks whether the screen feels right beyond passing its checks; a machine can only flag UI strings that rename standard objects against the journey's glossary.

exceptions: Quality is not perfection; start rough and iterate behind a quality bar with beta users

viewpoints.claim: Spend delight on rare moments, keep daily actions plain, and never let an element visibly duplicate itself during a transition.

source.author: Benji Taylor
source.quote: the potential for delight increases as the frequency of feature usage decreases

prefers: Directional motion between tabs
Morphing labels such as Continue to Confirm
One action per tray

measure.what: After a transition, count DOM nodes with the same key or text present twice on screen at once; frequency-weighted motion needs the journey to say what is frequent.
measure.mustFail: A list transition that clones the row and leaves both visible for a frame.
measure.mustPass: The original node moves.

exceptions: Utility, performance and security come first; delight is selective emphasis
viewpoints.kindsWhy: A landing page is a rare visit by definition and a docs page is read rather than acted on, so the frequency half of the rule collapses there; only the duplicate-node check applies.

viewpoints.claim: Reuse known controls, gestures and semantics; a novel interaction needs a standard alternative and a reason.

source.author: Scott Berkun
source.work: The future of UI will be boring
source.quote: The rookie trap designers and technologists fall for is confusing cool with useful

prefers: Native semantics and known gestures
An anchor for every link
Standard menus and selects
forbids: Novel gestures without a tap or keyboard alternative

measure.what: Custom widgets acting as select or menu with no role or keyboard handling fail; wheel or overscroll listeners calling preventDefault on document warn; drag-only affordances with no button alternative fail.
measure.mustFail: A <div class="dropdown"> with click-only open.
measure.mustPass: A <select> or an APG-conformant listbox.

exceptions: Deliberate departures with a point of view in place before the first component went down

viewpoints.claim: A library or AI default is someone else's decision; commit to one written aesthetic direction instead of inheriting it.

source.author: hipuku
source.work: The Default Is Not a Design Decision
source.quote: The default was always a design decision. Someone made it upstream, and everyone who builds on top inherits it without asking why.

prefers: A written token set such as DESIGN.md
One committed aesthetic direction
Semantic colour
forbids: Clean and modern as a brief
The AI-look constellation of purple gradient, Inter, identical cards, glass glow and bounce hover

measure.what: Score the constellation: purple-to-blue/cyan gradients warn, Inter or Roboto with no display face notes, 3+ identical icon+h3+p cards note, backdrop-filter plus glow notes, gradient text on numerals warns, overshoot cubic-bezier on hover warns.
measure.mustFail: A hero with linear-gradient(135deg,#7c3aed,#06b6d4), Inter, three glass cards and bounce hover.
measure.mustPass: The same layout with a single brand hue, no glass and ease-out hover.

exceptions: A purple brand is allowed to be purple; the tell is the constellation and the absence of a decision, not any one colour
